_comment: Names that two or more of the three vocabulary sources both claim to know,
and disagree about -- read by scripts/contract_parity.py.
py    backend/src/semantic_layer/models.py     StrEnum, the wire format
pkg   packages/semantic-types/src/*.ts         the published TS contract
Every entry here is a REAL divergence today, kept so the gate passes now and
fails on any NEW one. The list only shrinks: an entry that no longer diverges
fails the gate until it is removed, and an entry added since the merge base
Measured 2026-09-24 at f8f7d0f. Three divergences existed; CausalEntityType
was closed in the same change by adding OTHER to the TypeScript union, which
was a plain omission. The two that remain are not omissions -- the frontend
declares a different vocabulary, so closing them is a behaviour change to the
UI and needs its own commit. Both are on

ReviewStatus.why: The frontend renders a review lifecycle the backend does not emit. UNDER_REVIEW, APPROVED and ESCALATED are never sent by any endpoint; ACCEPTED and CONTESTED are sent and the frontend has no branch for them. The UI's states appear to be conflated with FragmentApprovalStatus (DRAFT/APPROVED/DEPRECATED), which is a different enum about a different object.
ReviewStatus.closes_by: Deciding which lifecycle is real, in the backend, and making the frontend narrow on that -- then deleting the local declaration and importing from @causalplatform/semantic-types.

EvidenceType.why: DOCUMENT_CITATION and METRIC_OBSERVATION exist in no backend enum; EXPERIMENT and SIMULATION are emitted and the frontend cannot represent them.
EvidenceType.closes_by: Deleting the local declaration and importing EvidenceType from @causalplatform/semantic-types, then fixing the call sites the compiler flags.
